# EfficientViM

**Category:** Efficient/Mobile · **Code:**
[`timm/models/efficientvim.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/pytorch-image-models/blob/main/timm/models/efficientvim.py)
· **Architectures:** 8 · **Pretrained weights:** 12 (0 with ImageNet-1k results)

Efficient Vision Mamba (EfficientViM) is built around the Hidden State Mixer based State Space Duality (HSM-SSD) layer,
implemented here in plain PyTorch. The `_dist` models add a distillation head.

## Papers

* [EfficientViM: Efficient Vision Mamba with Hidden State Mixer based State Space
  Duality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15241)

## Usage

See the [Quickstart](../quickstart) for loading pretrained weights, image preprocessing and fine-tuning, and [Feature
Extraction](../feature_extraction) for using the models as backbones.

```py
>>> import timm
>>> model = timm.create_model('efficientvim_m1.e300_in1k', pretrained=True)
>>> data_config = timm.data.resolve_model_data_config(model)
```

## Model API support

| Feature | `EfficientViM` | `EfficientViMDistilled` |
|---|---|---|
| [`features_only=True` feature maps](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ (strides 16, 32, 64) | ✓ (strides 16, 32, 64) |
| [`forward_intermediates()`](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`prune_intermediate_layers()`](../model_api#intermediate-features) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [Any input size, no changes needed](../model_api#input-size) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`set_input_size()`](../model_api#input-size) | – | – |
| [`dynamic_img_size=True`](../model_api#input-size) | – | – |
| [`set_grad_checkpointing()`](../model_api#training-hooks) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [Layer-wise LR decay (`group_matcher()`)](../model_api#training-hooks) | ✓ | ✓ |
| [`reset_classifier()`](../model_api#classifier) | ✓ | ✓ |

✓ supported, ✓ (square) works for square sizes only, ✗ not supported, – not needed (the model already accepts any input
size). Checked by running each feature on a randomly initialized model (`EfficientViM` with `efficientvim_m1` at 224,
`EfficientViMDistilled` with `efficientvim_m1_dist` at 224), other architectures of the same class are expected to
behave the same. See the [Model API](../model_api) page for details.
